text: Needs::Sweep streams where Needs::Count indexes, and the difference is what happens after the count: tail goes on to address the last records out of order, so it wants an offset table; skim reads forward from there, so an offset table would cost 16 bytes a record to spare a pass it can just take. An index file beside the input removes that pass either way, since index::count_in reads the count out of the 35-byte header, which is what makes sail index worth running first.
